episode.title: Corrections, Trust, and the Long Game

bullets: A correction is a reliability signal rather than a failure — a pattern observed at teams using BBC and NPR.
Ignoring corrections as a reliability signal carries a delayed cost; teams that do so end up rebuilding it from scratch a year later.
Managing the risk of being wrong in public is its own discipline, a pattern observed holding across three different teams.
Framing reliability around the risk of being wrong in public matters because it reveals which trade-offs are actually being made.
Risk management cross-cuts every other reliability concern — its trade-offs touch everything else rather than sitting in a separate silo.
Adoption works best through small experiments rather than wholesale change — pick one idea, run it for two weeks, and treat the rest as iteration.
